The CSM considered that fluid overload was the most important predisposing factor. Other risk factors included multiple pregnancies, a history of cardiac disease, and maternal infection. Pharmacokinetics Ritodrine is rapidly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract but is subject to fairly extensive first-pass metab- olism; about 30% of an oral dose is bioavailable. It is metabolised in the liver primarily by conjugation with glucuronic acid or sulfate and excreted in urine as un- changed drug and metabolites. About 70 to 90% of a dose is reported to be excreted in the urine within 10 to 12 hours. It crosses the placenta. ◊ References. 1. Gandar R, et al. Serum level of ritodrine in man.
